label: Copy phase, mid-copy (not first/last output), input is one of k o m x r n t p z h
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens or the delimiter, and almost never on the first fed-back token (recall_idx 1). Inside the copy phase it depends on which token is being fed back: k is strongest (22% rate, ~20% of mass; the top activations are mostly k fed back at recall_idx 2), then o and m, then x r n t p z h. e and i are weak. Rate is highest at recall_idx 2-3 (right after the first copied token) and at the late positions of long sequences (t 16-17). It is lower on the final output step (to_go 0) and on short sequences (L <= 5 rarely fire). It never fires on a token occurring for the first time in the sequence, which follows from the copy-phase restriction. Prev-token effects are weak: y a g e as prev_tok give about 2x lift. The token-set predicate gets about 0.76 of the activation mass, but precision is only about 0.39 because many copy steps with these tokens stay inactive. The activation looks like a graded mix of token identity and position, not a clean binary condition.
